forms.title: Thai e-Visa (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
forms.stoppedAt: Sign-in to a Thai e-Visa account (account creation needs personal data); the application steps are seen only by name in "How to apply online".

steps.name: Sign in
notices: You can sign in using your Thai E-Visa account to apply for a visa and track your application.

Attention : E-Visa applicants are no longer required to submit passports and supporting documents in person at the Royal Thai Embassy/Consulate-General. It is important to note that you are only able to apply if you are currently not in Thailand. After the e-Visa application has been approved, a confirmation e-mail will be sent to applicants, which can be printed out for presenting to airlines and Thai immigration officials when traveling to Thailand.

*All applications are subject to approval and the Royal Thai Embassy or Consulate-General may request for an interview or additional documents. Submission of a visa application does not necessarily mean that a visa will be granted. Please also note that the visa fees are non-refundable.

steps.name: Wait for the visa to be processed
e-Visa confirmation document sent by email

forms.title: Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) (Immigration Bureau)
forms.stoppedAt: "Arrival Card" is gated by a Cloudflare Turnstile check that does not complete in our browser; the form route (#/tac/arrival-card) renders blank without it.

steps.name: Important notice
notices: In accordance to Immigration Act, B.E. 2522
1. All passengers must complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card.

2. If the alien stays in the Kingdom longer than 90 days, he/she must notify in writing the nearest Immigration Officer, concerning place of stay, as soon as possible upon expiration of 90 days. And required to do so every 90 days.
3. Aliens are not allowed to work unless they are granted Work Permit.
4. Foreigners are required to submit their arrival card information 3 days in advance of their arrival date in Thailand.
